question: An 18-year-old Caucasian female presents to your clinic because of a recent increase in thirst and hunger. Urinalysis demonstrates elevated glucose. The patient's BMI is 20. Which of the following is the most common cause of death in persons suffering from this patient's illness?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Increased thirst and hunger" -> "Elevated glucose in urinalysis" -> "Diagnosis of diabetes mellitus" -> "Increased risk of cardiovascular diseases" -> "Myocardial infarction" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Elevated glucose in urinalysis" -> "Diagnosis of diabetes mellitus" -> "Poorly controlled diabetes" -> "Increased risk of infections" -> "Infection" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Diagnosis of diabetes mellitus" -> "Poorly controlled diabetes" -> "Peripheral neuropathy" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Diagnosis of diabetes mellitus" -> "Poorly controlled diabetes" -> "Hyperglycemic crisis" -> "Coma" -> 50%
analysis: The patient is likely presenting with symptoms of diabetes mellitus, given the elevated glucose levels and symptoms of increased thirst and hunger. The most common cause of death in persons suffering from diabetes mellitus is cardiovascular disease, particularly myocardial infarction.
